description: Lethbridge Polytechnic offers entrance awards to students admitted to full-time programs at the institution. With over 400 awards worth $800,000+ available through a single application, this is a major scholarship opportunity for qualifying students. Alberta residents can also apply for provincial scholarships (Jason Lang and Louise McKinney) using the same application.

title: Voice for Animals High School Scholarship
audience: High school students ages 14-18 who advocate for animal welfare
notes: Two age categories: 14-15 and 16-18. Submit essay or short video on animal welfare, species extinction, or reducing animal suffering. 21 awards total.
description: The Voice for Animals High School Scholarship awards up to $500 to 21 high school students (ages 14-18) who demonstrate passion for animal welfare. Applicants submit a written essay or short video addressing topics such as animal mistreatment, species extinction, or solutions to animal suffering. The contest is divided into two age categories (14-15 and 16-18 years), giving younger and older high school students equal footing. No citizenship requirement.

title: Luke Santi Memorial Award
audience: Graduating Canadian high school students entering physical sciences
notes: Minimum 80% final-year average. Must be accepted into a full-time physical sciences program at a Canadian university. Includes an invitation to visit the Perimeter Institute.
description: The Luke Santi Memorial Award honours a graduating high school student who embodies excellence in the physical sciences. Named for a passionate young scientist, this $1,000 award from the Perimeter Institute requires a minimum 80% average and acceptance into a full-time physical sciences program at a Canadian university. Applicants must demonstrate scientific curiosity, extracurricular involvement, and community contributions. Two letters of recommendation are required. The recipient also receives an invitation to visit the Perimeter Institute for Theoretical Physics.

title: Stuck at Prom Scholarship
audience: High school students who create a prom outfit using Duck Brand duct tape
notes: Grand prize is $10,000 per couple (2 winners). Runner-up prizes are $1,000 each (8 winners). Create a prom dress or tuxedo using Duck Brand duct tape. Parental consent required for applicants under 18. Quebec residents are ineligible.
description: The Stuck at Prom Scholarship by Duck Brand challenges high school students to create their prom outfit entirely from Duck Brand duct tape. Entries are judged on workmanship, originality, use of colours and accessories, and creative use of tape. The grand prize is $10,000 (awarded to each member of the winning couple), with runner-up prizes of $1,000 each for 8 additional winners. Canadian residents (excluding Quebec) who are currently enrolled in high school are eligible. Parental or guardian consent is required for applicants under 18.

title: Fraser Institute Student Essay Contest
audience: Canadian high school students interested in economics and public policy
notes: Write a 1,000–1,500 word essay on what a Fraser Institute Essential Scholar would say about Canadian economic prosperity today. Include school name and grade. Academic references required.
description: The Fraser Institute Student Essay Contest invites Canadian high school students to engage with ideas from the Fraser Institute's Essential Scholars series. Contestants write a 1,000–1,500 word essay exploring what one of those thinkers would say about Canadian economic prosperity today. Up to 15 awards of $1,500 are available across high school, undergraduate, and graduate categories. High school submissions must include the school name and grade. Strong essays demonstrate economic reasoning and cite academic references.

title: Valour Canada History and Heritage Scholarship
audience: Canadian youth under 21 not currently enrolled in post-secondary
notes: Must be under 21 as of June 30, 2026 and not attending post-secondary between Sept 1, 2025 and Aug 13, 2026. Quebec residents ineligible. Submit a written statement and a 4–6 minute YouTube video visiting a local Canadian war memorial.
description: The Valour Canada History and Heritage Scholarship recognizes Canadian youth who engage with their country's military history and service. Applicants under 21 who are not currently in post-secondary education submit a 4–6 minute YouTube video visiting a local war memorial or monument, referencing at least two of Valour Canada's character pillars (communication, cooperation, courage, responsibility, resilience, or thoughtfulness), along with a short written statement. The top prize is $2,000; a runner-up award of $500 is also given. Quebec residents and those attending post-secondary during the 2025-2026 school year are not eligible.

title: Communication Contest for the Deaf and Hard of Hearing
audience: High school students with certified hearing loss of 40+ decibels
notes: Requires audiogram from a qualified audiologist (completed within 24 months) showing 40+ decibel hearing loss. Compete via speech or sign language on the topic: "The Moment I Realized I Belonged — My Definition of Community." Sponsored by local Optimist Club chapters.
description: The Optimist International Communication Contest for the Deaf and Hard of Hearing awards $2,500 to high school students who demonstrate communication skills despite certified hearing challenges. Contestants must have a documented hearing loss of 40 decibels or more (verified by audiogram within the past 24 months) and present a speech or sign language performance on the 2025-2026 topic: "The Moment I Realized I Belonged — My Definition of Community." The contest is organized at the local district level through Optimist Club chapters across Canada, the US, and the Caribbean, with up to 45 awards available.

title: Breakthrough Junior Challenge
audience: Students ages 13–18 worldwide
description: Create a short video (2 minutes or less) explaining a big idea from life sciences, physics, or math. The winner receives a $250,000 scholarship, their teacher receives $50,000, and their school receives a $100,000 science lab. Winners are celebrated at the Breakthrough Prize Ceremony.

title: China-Alberta Award for Excellence in Chinese
audience: Alberta Grade 12 students who have completed Chinese Language and Culture 10 and 20
description: The China-Alberta Award for Excellence in Chinese recognizes Alberta Grade 12 students who excel in the Chinese Language and Culture Program. Applicants must have completed Chinese Language and Culture 10 and 20 and be currently enrolled in or have completed level 30, with a minimum 80% average across all courses and a minimum 90% average in Chinese Language and Culture 10 and 20. The application includes a two-paragraph essay on how the program will apply to the student's future studies or career. Only Canadian citizens, permanent residents, or protected persons who are Alberta residents (with at least one parent residing in Alberta) are eligible; visa students do not qualify.
